chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man swears three oaths while being truthful and intending to break them, he must shed blood (pay a fine). And when he swears one oath while being a liar, he has disputed (with God), and he must shed blood (pay a fine).

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one who intends to break the oath / one who makes the oath binding

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the specific expiation (*dam*) for oaths, distinguishing between the severity of breaking three oaths while truthful but intending to break them, versus breaking a single oath while lying. The term 'shed blood' (*yuhariquhu*) is interpreted by Shia jurists as a monetary fine, typically equivalent to the value of a camel, sheep, or goat, reflecting the practical application of *kaffarah* in daily life. This hadith underscores the importance of intention (*niyyah*) and truthfulness in vow-making, a key theme in Shia fiqh regarding the binding nature of oaths.
